Bootstrap likelihood-ratio test of K-1 against K classes (Mplus TECH14)

blrt.Rd

Parametric bootstrap likelihood-ratio test (McLachlan 1987; McLachlan & Peel 2000) of the fitted K-class model against K-1 classes.

Usage

blrt(object, reps = 100, seed = 20261120)

Arguments

object

A fitted latentmix model with K >= 2 classes, without weights or covariates.

reps

Number of bootstrap samples.

seed

Random seed.

Value

An object of class c("latentmix_blrt", "latentmix_aux"), a list with h0_ll, lr (observed 2 times log-likelihood difference), df, p (bootstrap p-value), reps, lr_boot (the bootstrap statistics), K and text.

Details

The K-1 class model is fitted to the data; reps data sets are generated from it (keeping each case's missing-data pattern), and both models are fitted to each with their own random starts (20/4 for K-1 and 40/8 for K classes; Mplus LRTSTARTS default is 0 0 40 8). The p-value is the share of bootstrap statistics at least as large as the observed one. Replications run in parallel on the Julia threads (see lm_start()). Not available with sampling weights, covariates or a complex survey design (cluster/strata; Mplus TECH14 is not available with TYPE = MIXTURE COMPLEX).

References

McLachlan, G. J. (1987). On bootstrapping the likelihood ratio test statistic for the number of components in a normal mixture. Applied Statistics, 36(3), 318–324. doi:10.2307/2347790

McLachlan, G., & Peel, D. (2000). Finite Mixture Models. Wiley. doi:10.1002/0471721182

Nylund, K. L., Asparouhov, T., & Muthén, B. O. (2007). Deciding on the number of classes in latent class analysis and growth mixture modeling: A Monte Carlo simulation study. Structural Equation Modeling, 14(4), 535–569. doi:10.1080/10705510701575396

See also

lmr(), fittable(), lm_table() (blrt argument of the fit comparison).

Examples

data(wellbeing)
# \donttest{
# Do three wellbeing profiles fit better than two? Bootstrap LRT (Mplus TECH14)
p3 <- lpa(wellbeing, sleep:lifesat, K = 3, variances = "varying")
#> Starting Julia ...
b <- blrt(p3, reps = 100)
b   # p < 0.05: keep (at least) three profiles
#> ━━ Bootstrap likelihood-ratio test: 2 vs. 3 classes ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
#>   H0 log-likelihood (K - 1 classes)  -10431.972
#>   2 × LL difference                     567.478
#>   Difference in parameters                   13
#>   Bootstrap samples                         100
#>   Bootstrap p                            <0.001
# }
